title: Inventory Evidence Sequence Persistence Prerequisite
selectedSlice: C — shared monotonic inventory evidence sequence persistence prerequisite
purpose: Define, but do not execute, a migration that gives production-batch and physical-inventory-movement persistence one shared append-only monotonic evidence registration sequence for later stable-cutoff enumeration.
rules: A single shared sequence namespace covers both production batches and physical inventory movements.
The sequence is assigned by durable persistence registration, not by business date, lexical identifier ordering or caller input.
The sequence is positive, monotonic and bounded to JavaScript safe-integer range.
Production-batch inserts automatically append one ledger entry.
Physical-inventory-movement inserts automatically append one ledger entry.
Existing rows are backfilled if this migration is eventually executed after data already exists.
Backfill ordering is deterministic but does not claim historical insertion chronology.
The ledger is append-only and rejects update and delete.
The ledger binds evidence family, exact SKU, exact batch identity and movement identity where applicable.
Supporting indexes permit future exact-SKU evidence enumeration through an explicit sequence cutoff.
Supporting indexes permit future exact-batch movement evidence enumeration through an explicit sequence cutoff.
This slice creates no read API and does not acquire a cutoff.
This slice does not establish manifest completeness.
This slice does not establish a point-in-time inventory snapshot.
This slice does not establish authoritative current quantity-on-hand.
This slice does not establish availability, capacity, checkout, payment, fulfillment, accounting or rewards authority.
Migration 0005 must not be executed in this slice.
Migrations 0003 and 0004 remain unchanged and unexecuted.
laterUse: Acquire a durable evidence high-water sequence.
Enumerate every exact-SKU ledger entry with evidence_sequence less than or equal to that cutoff.
Resolve exact canonical batch and movement evidence.
Bind the cutoff and complete evidence manifest together.
Only later evaluate whether complete-through-cutoff recorded balance can participate in authoritative inventory semantics.
